children: said on Wednesday U.S.-based Wildcat Infrastructure had offered to buy its U.S. business for up to $1.35 billion, topping a bid from South Korea's Hanwha Group tabled last month.
Shares of Australia's biggest shipbuilder jumped as much as 9% to a month-high of A$4.74, as of 0110 GMT.
Hanwha proposed to buy the U.S. operations for up to $1.20 billion a month ago as the South Korean conglomerate looks to expand in the American defence market.
Wildcat offered to buy the operations for between $1.25 billion and $1.35 billion on a cash and debt-free basis and is subject to four weeks of due diligence.
Miami-based Wildcat indicated it intended to operate the company as a standalone platform, retaining the Austal brand and the U.S. operations.
Hanwha Group declined to comment when contacted by Reuters.
